observations.text: Reviewed bytes are commit 0c89ef3 with a clean tree: git status --porcelain printed nothing before and after this review, so the judged oracle and support bytes are the committed ones.

Mechanical selection, recorded as run: argv "git diff --name-status ad7687c..0c89ef3" exit 0 named the test files changed since the last approval: tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs (the S1 oracle), tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs (declared support), tests/acceptance/review_app_sign_in_and_ownership.rs (uses the moved SCAN_ACTIONS constant) and tests/acceptance/review_app_legacy_run_repos_read.rs (S2, out of this slice). argv "code-fact impacted-tests tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs tests/acceptance/support/review_app/app.rs --root ." exit 0 but printed EMPTY stdout and no stderr: the port returned no selection, so it is reported as an empty answer, not as none impacted, and selection fell back to the declared verification command for S1.

GREEN run, this commit: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/jeffbailey/.cache/nwdes/fix-repos-read-truthful/target-ad, argv "cargo test --offline -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure -- --nocapture", exit 0, stdout "test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 5.00s", no stderr, wall 5 s on this Mac host. Both S1 scenarios and the two harness state-delta controls ran.

Semantic RED observed by this reviewer, not reported: the resume guard at crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs:555-557 was replaced by "let _ = record_checks(app, owner_did, run_id, &checked);", then argv "cargo test --offline -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure" exit 101, stdout "test result: FAILED. 3 passed; 1 failed ... finished in 4.38s", failing test a_scan_that_cannot_save_that_it_read_a_repo_is_offered_for_resuming, panic at tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:157 with left "completed" and right "interrupted". That is the business assertion of the promised outcome, not a compile, collection, fixture or startup failure. The mutation was reverted with "git checkout -- crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs" and git status --porcelain is empty again; no proptest regression file was left behind.

The added step is not redundant coverage: under the same mutation the second scenario a_scan_that_cannot_save_her_account_checks_is_offered_for_resuming stayed green, because its refusal is met on the fresh-scan path (scan.rs:458). Only the new middle pick-up, under a store that still refuses saving her account checks, falsifies a dropped error on the resume path. It maps to the declared S1 falsifier, the run ends Completed after a refused store write, and to promise P1.

Obligation closure for S1 holds in both directions. E1 (interrupted, never Completed) is asserted three times: on the fresh-scan path for each refused write, and on the resume path for the picked-up run. E2 (resumable, picks the same run up) is asserted by then_her_queue_offers_only_resume_and_claims_no_count before every pick-up, which requires "Resume scan" and refuses both fresh-scan actions, followed by a pick-up that completes. E3 (no untrue repos-read count) is asserted by the no-wording check on every interrupted queue and by then_her_queue_counts_exactly, whose counts_claimed reads the whole number in front of each wording so an over-count ending in the true number is read as the number it is. No oracle observation lacks a declared obligation.

The refactor preserves the observation it moved. The earlier version asserted inside the resume step that the queue offered "Resume scan" and no fresh-scan action; the current when_she_picks_the_run_up only presses and waits, while the same assertion is now a Then step called immediately before every pick-up. Because when_scan_finishes presses whichever of SCAN_ACTIONS is offered, that preceding Then is what pins the pressed action to "Resume scan". Nothing is weakened and the step now holds exactly one stimulus.

The printed evidence matches the assertions at every judging moment, read from the GREEN run with --nocapture. After the first scan: status interrupted, status region "Your last scan was interrupted. The suggestions found so far are kept; press Resume scan to finish it.", repos-read line ABSENT, scan actions offered "Resume scan". After the middle pick-up with the store still refusing: "(no repo was read)", status interrupted, repos-read line ABSENT, scan actions offered "Resume scan". After the final pick-up: three repos read (priyaraman/estuary, priyaraman/quill-docs, priyaraman/tidepool), status completed, status region "3 repos read", scan actions offered "Scan again". The first scan of that scenario read priyaraman/tidepool, which the final pick-up read again, so no repo whose read was never saved was skipped.

Advisory, owner oracle, non-blocking: the final pick-up assertions (it read at least one repo, and the queue counts exactly what it read) hold because the middle pick-up meets its refused write before reading any repo, which the run shows as "(no repo was read)". The closed design does not fix that order between recording the account checks and marking repos read, so an equivalent implementation that recorded the checks after reading would mark reads in the middle pick-up and make the final pick-up read nothing while still telling the owner the truth. The assertion is true of the agreed behaviour today and is kept; a later reordering returns here rather than to the crafter.

Advisory, owner oracle, non-blocking: FRESH_SCAN_LABELS in the oracle restates, as SCAN_AGAIN plus SCAN_MY_REPOS, the fact that those are the scan actions other than "Resume scan", while SCAN_ACTIONS now lives in the support. A fourth scan action added to the support would be excluded by neither. No observation is lost today.

Retained from the accepted examination at ad7687c and unchanged by this delta: the suites never print a run identifier, so the picked-up run is attested by its heading rather than by an id, and the suggestions the cut-short run kept are not asserted. Those limits were judged sufficient then and this delta does not touch them; they are not reopened.

Timing: no per-test or feature budget and no derogation are declared for this feature, so no budget judgment is made. The measured facts are the whole declared selection finishing in 5.00 s of test time (4 tests, 5 s wall) at this commit and 4.38 s under the mutation, with the delta adding one app restart to one scenario. No infrastructure suite exists or is proposed.

diagnostic: Accepted: the revised S1 oracle is public, independent and complete for P1, and its new observation was proved falsifiable by this reviewer. Re-review was limited to the delta since ad7687c (the shared queue wordings in the support, the show_repos_read evidence, and the pick-up under a store that still refuses a write) and to the obligations E1, E2 and E3 those touch; the earlier judgments and the accepted examination limits are retained. Every stimulus and observation goes through the public HTTP port on a development build with the declared fault seam, with only GitHub and the ATProto network faked. Semantic RED observed here: with the resume guard at crates/openlore-review-app/src/scan.rs:555-557 replaced by let _ =, the oracle fails at review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:157 on left "completed" against right "interrupted", while the other scenario stays green, so the added middle pick-up is the only falsifier of a dropped error on the resume path; restored and the tree is clean. Unmutated, the declared command is exit 0 with 4 passed in 5.00 s. No findings. Two non-blocking advisories stay with the oracle owner: the final pick-up assertions rely on the middle refusal being met before any repo is read, which the closed design does not fix, and FRESH_SCAN_LABELS restates a fact the support now owns. Craft is not blocked; nothing here is owed by design, implementation or product. typesafe: unavailable (no API key in this environment); the mechanical impacted-tests query returned an empty answer with exit 0, so selection used the declared verification command.
